body:
`dispatch_annotation_deletes` (cps/services/annotation_sync/__init__.py:705) is the
Kobo PATCH `deletedAnnotationIds` handler. It selects the row to soft-delete on
`user_id` + `annotation_id` only:

    query = ub.session.query(ub.Annotation).filter(
        ub.Annotation.user_id == user.id,
        ub.Annotation.annotation_id == annotation_id,
    )

There is no provenance check. A Kobo device can therefore soft-delete a
`webreader` or `koreader` row in a single push.

This is the same class as F-1927e0 / #1790 (a delete path with no source
authority), in the one spelling of delete that was never re-checked when those
landed. It is strictly easier to reach than F-1927e0, which needed two pushes
and a provenance flip; this needs one push naming the id.

WHY THE DEVICE CANNOT HONESTLY KNOW THE ID
Annotation writeback to the device is not implemented: `serveable` on
`KoboAnnotationMaterialization` is hardcoded `False` at both write sites
(annotation_sync/__init__.py:374, :389) and is never set true anywhere in the
tree. No annotation is ever served back to a Kobo device, so a Kobo device
provably never held a `webreader`/`koreader` row, and naming one in
`deletedAnnotationIds` is not reachable by honest use.

ASYMMETRY WITH THE KOREADER BRIDGE
The KOReader bridge does the same operation gated by
`_DELETABLE_SOURCES = {"koreader"}`
(progress_syncing/protocols/koreader_annotations.py:67, :390). Both bridges
receive all sources on pull; only one may delete across sources. One of the two
is wrong, and the unrestricted one is the Kobo path.

RECOVERABILITY
The docstring claims "Recovery is symmetric: a subsequent create/update PATCH
for the same annotation_id un-hides it." That recovery is available only to a
Kobo device. A web-reader row hidden this way has no un-hide affordance in the
web UI, so for the user it is unrecoverable through any application path — the
same severity note that set #1790's rating.

OBSERVED PROOF (in-memory ub schema, dispatch_annotation_deletes called directly)
    BEFORE: kobo-1(kobo,False)  web-1(webreader,False)  kor-1(koreader,False)
    AFTER : kobo-1(kobo,True)   web-1(webreader,True)   kor-1(koreader,True)
    FOREIGN ROWS DESTROYED BY A KOBO DELETE: ['web-1', 'kor-1']

WHY THE FIX IS SAFE
The Kobo PATCH create path only ever assigns `source="kobo"`
(annotation_sync/__init__.py:294), and the KoboReader.sqlite importer also
writes `source="kobo"`. Restricting this path's delete authority to `{"kobo"}`
therefore cannot affect any honest Kobo delete.

FORWARD NOTE
If annotation writeback (F-3b565b, design-only) is ever implemented, the
device would legitimately hold foreign rows and this authority model must be
revisited deliberately rather than by default.

resolution.note: Fixed and merged as #1793. dispatch_annotation_deletes now takes a REQUIRED keyword-only deletable_sources; Kobo PATCH passes {'kobo'}, KOReader passes _DELETABLE_SOURCES, the authenticated web-reader delete passes None (user authority across provenance). Verified on merged main: the original proof now shows both foreign rows surviving while the honest kobo delete still lands, refusals logged with provenance. Degrading the guard to constant-true (exactly the pre-fix behaviour) fails test_kobo_delete_authority_refuses_foreign_sources_and_fans_out_owned. /security-review returned no findings at confidence >=8 and independently confirmed the None sentinel is unreachable from any device path and that no other writer bypasses the gate.

title: Kobo PATCH deletedAnnotationIds has no provenance authority: one push soft-deletes webreader and koreader rows
